title: Local demographic reorganization does not scale into a transferable island-resilience rule in Antarctic penguins
central_claim: Local demographic organization can be strong and repeatable without becoming transferable information in static island traits at macroecological scales.

part_I.claim: Palmer Adélie decline is accompanied by within-island concentration beyond proportional thinning plus prespecified count error.

part_II.primary: 2 km A x H cross-species median gamma_AH = -0.318; permutation p = 0.0947; non-confirmatory
part_II.simple_buffering: A-only negative in all three species but no Holm-adjusted rejection
part_II.MDE: MDE80 |gamma_AH|=0.498; MDE90=0.539; moderate effects near observed magnitude remain weakly detectable
part_II.radius: joint 2-to-5 km sign-switch-plus-contrast null p=0.081; describe as radius sensitivity, not biological scale dependence

narrative_changes_from_v0_1: Abstract foregrounds cross-scale asymmetry rather than two separate papers.
Introduction reframes the paper as transferability of island information across hierarchical scales.
Estimator-development history is compressed to a single Methods paragraph; detailed failures remain Supplement/provenance.
Discussion opening now treats the result as a boundary on information transfer rather than a local-positive/broad-negative contrast.
Conclusion distinguishes strong local organization from weak transferability of static island descriptors.
All principal equations were normalized to clean LaTeX markup.
